title: Civil Affairs Medical Sergeant (CA Medical SGT) (Active Component Only)
raw_text:
10-38W. MOS 38W—Civil Affairs Medical Sergeant (CA Medical SGT) (Active Component Only),
CMF 38 (Eff 202410)
    a. Major duties. The Civil Affairs (CA) Medical Sergeant conducts medical mission planning and
performs advanced emergency medical treatment and prolonged field care in austere environments on a
four-person Civil Affairs Team (CAT). The Civil Affairs Medical Sergeant provides field sanitation
assessments, evaluates medical systems and infrastructure, conducts civil network engagement, medical
reconnaissance, and provides situational understanding to transitional governments. These functions
provide situational understanding, targeting data, information operations, freedom of maneuver, and
stability. They shape the operational environment, affect the civil component, preserve combat power,
maintain operating tempo, and consolidate gains by supporting Transitional Governance. The Civil Affairs
Medical Sergeant performs their principal duties in hostile, denied, or politically sensitive environments.
Duties of MOS 38BW at each level of skill are:
          (1) MOSC 38W1O. (Personnel Only). MOS used to identify Soldiers accessed into MOS 38W
prior to obtaining grade SSG.
          (2) MOSC 38W2O. (Personnel Only). MOS used to identify Soldiers accessed into MOS 38W
prior to obtaining grade SSG.
          (3) MOSC 38W3O. Provides medical, language, and regional expertise as part of a CAT.
Conducts medical mission planning and performs advanced emergency medical treatment and prolonged
field care in austere environments on a four-person Civil Affairs Team (CAT). Provides field sanitation
assessments, evaluates medical systems and infrastructure, conducts civil network engagement, medical
reconnaissance, and provides situational understanding to transitional governments.
    b. Physical demands rating and qualification for initial award of MOS. Civil Affairs Medical Sergeant
must possess the following qualifications:
          (1) A physical demands rating of Significant (Gray).
          (2) A physical profile of 111221.
          (3) Qualifying scores.
              (a) A minimum score of 110 in aptitude area GT.
              (b) A minimum score of 101 in aptitude area ST.
          (4) A minimum OPAT score of Long Jump (LJ) – 0120 cm, Seated Power Throw (PT) – 0350 cm,
Strength Deadlift (SD) – 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 0036 shuttles in Physical Demand
Category “Significant” (Gray).
          (5) Must be airborne qualified and maintain SQI P Parachutist or volunteer to attend Basic
Airborne Course.
          (6) Must be Survival, Evasion, Resistance, and Escape Level C (SERE-C) graduate effective on
and after 1 October 2024.
          (7) A minimum-security eligibility of SECRET is required for the initial award and to maintain the
MOS.
          (8) A U.S. citizen or naturalized citizen.
          (9) High school graduate or GED certificate.
          (10) Must maintain a current, valid, unrestricted National Registry Emergency Medical Technician
(NREMT) Certification and USSOCOM Advanced Tactical Paramedic (ATP) Certification to retain MOS
38W.
          (11) Not barred to reenlist IAW AR 601-280, or under suspension of favorable personnel action
IAW AR 600-8-2.
          (12) No history of a qualifying military or civilian conviction of a crime of domestic violence, as
defined by AR 600-20, Army Command Policy, paragraph 4-22.
          (13) No history of any use of an illicit substance following the Soldier's date of initial entry into
military service.
          (14) No history of any use of a controlled substance without a valid prescription following the
Soldier's date of initial entry into military service.
          (15) No history of a military or civilian charge for Driving Under the Influence or Reckless Driving.
          (16) No history of any other open military or civilian administrative or criminal investigation,
charge, or indictment on the Soldier.
          (17) No record of conviction by special or general courts-martial or civilian courts of offenses
listed in AR 27-10 (Military Justice) chapter 24 or otherwise required to register as a sexual offender
under AR 27-10, chapter 24.

                (a) Active Component Soldiers: Must be in grade E4/SPC with Basic Leadership Course
 (BLC) completion and a minimum of 12 months of Active Federal Service through E6/SSG with no more
 than 10 years Active Federal Service (waivable by the Civil Affairs Proponent) and must meet the
 prerequisites IAW AR 614-200 to include successful attendance and selection at the Civil Affairs
 Assessment and Selection Course (CAAS) (non-waivable).
                (b) Formal Training: Active Component Soldiers must successfully complete the Civil Affairs
Assessment and Selection Course (CAAS), Basic Airborne Course (if not already qualified), Special
Operations Combat Medic Course (SOCM), Survival, Evasion, Resistance, and Escape Level C (SERE-
C), Civil Affairs Medical Sergeants Phase I and Phase II Courses, Civil Affairs Sluss-Tiller Course, Basic
Special Operations Language Training and Civil Affairs Medical Sergeants Phase III Course conducted
under the auspices of the U.S. Army John F. Kennedy Special Warfare Center and School
(USAJFKSWCS).
           (19) Accessions. Initial entry trainee must complete the 12B10-OSUT (Combat Engineer) course,
Civil Affairs Preparation and Conditioning Course, Civil Affairs Assessment and Selection Course (CAAS),
Basic Airborne Course, Basic Leadership Course (BLC), Special Operations Combat Medic Course
(SOCM), Survival, Evasion, Resistance, and Escape Level C (SERE C), Civil Affairs Medical Sergeants
Phase I and Phase II Courses, Civil Affairs Sluss-Tiller Course, Basic Special Operations Language
Training and Civil Affairs Medical Sergeants Phase III Course conducted under the auspices of the U.S.
Army John F. Kennedy Special Warfare Center and School (USAJFKSWCS).
      c. Additional skill identifiers (ASIs): J8 Government Support Element (GSE) (Effective 202310) (Refer

matches: Coordinate work with other emergency medical team members or police or fire department personnel.

The Civil Affairs (CA) Medical Sergeant conducts medical mission planning and performs advanced emergency medical treatment and prolonged field care in austere environments on a four-person Civil Affairs Team (CAT).
Study operations sequence, material flow, functional statements, organization charts, and project information to determine worker functions and responsibilities.
These functions provide situational understanding, targeting data, information operations, freedom of maneuver, and stability.
Discuss medical health of pets with clients, such as post-operative status.
Provides medical, language, and regional expertise as part of a CAT.
Instruct emergency medical response team about emergency interventions to ensure correct application of procedures.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
